requirements.text: The SCE-MI shall provide a standard C/C++ modeling interface for connecting software models on a host workstation to structural hardware models (DUT) on an emulation platform.
The interface shall support multiple communication channels between software models and hardware transactors.
The interface shall support message-oriented communication (transactions) rather than event-oriented communication.
The interface shall provide a mechanism for hardware transactors to control the DUT clock (controlled time) and suspend it during message processing.
The interface shall provide a service loop function to allow the SCE-MI infrastructure to process queued messages in both single-threaded and multi-threaded environments.
The hardware side shall provide macros for message input ports, message output ports, clock control, and clock generation.
The software side shall provide C++ objects and methods for version discovery, parameter access, initialization, binding, and message dispatching.
The interface shall be optimized to avoid communication bottlenecks and minimize throttling of the emulator.
The interface shall support high-speed verification by allowing a single message to trigger multiple clocked events in the hardware.
The interface shall support plug-and-play transactor models to hide the complexity of the SCE-MI from end users.
The interface shall provide a C API for compatibility with non-C++ applications.
The interface shall provide a standardized error handling mechanism for reporting issues during co-modeling sessions.
